elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 4.1: "unless terminated by the Company for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI" — the Company (Customer) now has an express convenience right; the Agreement has no Order Form construct, so agreement-level right suffices.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice remains "ninety (90) days written notice to HDI"; no 30-day alternative is offered.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund obligation anywhere in the rendered text; instead the Company still owes a Termination Payment under 4.2(a)/(c) (as capped).

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "HDI may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term" — no convenience termination can take effect during a committed term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: 4.1 as edited: "terminated by the Company for convenience and without cause upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI" — 90 days is at the outer edge of the 60–90 day band; retained sentence "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" preserves the Company's ability to fix the effective date.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Added: "In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments due from the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." This caps the 4.2(a) formula at three months of Section 3.1 fees without disturbing the 4.2(c) instalment mechanics.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "HDI may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term"; HDI was simultaneously removed from the "either Party" convenience trigger in 4.1, so no unconfined HDI convenience exit survives.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence: "upon ninety (90) days written notice to the Company."

reasons: Fallback level is complete in operative language: express Customer convenience right at 90 days, HDI convenience exit confined to end of then-current term on 90 days' notice, and a hard three-month cap on the Termination Payment.

Preferred fails on two elements the drafter correctly declines to press: notice is 90 rather than 30 days, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund (the Company still pays a capped Termination Payment).

Minimal: three surgical operations, each traceable to a fallback element. No survival tail, no at-own-expense language, no new procedures, and the favourable retained sentences (Termination Date specification, 4.2(c) quarterly instalments) are untouched.

Intent preserved: the 4.2(a) formula and 4.2(c) payment schedule survive intact under an "In no event shall ... exceed" cap, the "Termination Date" definition still has its source in 4.1, and the Section 3.1 cross-reference resolves.

Non-blocking observation for the drafter: because the Company's convenience right still sits inside the auto-renewal sentence ("shall be automatically renewed ... unless terminated by the Company for convenience"), a counterparty could argue it is only a non-renewal right. The retained "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated" sentence cuts against that reading, but a standalone sentence would remove the ambiguity if the point is contested.

Non-blocking observation: the deletion of "either Party" from 4.1 removes HDI's non-cause exit from that sentence only; HDI's for-cause termination rights elsewhere are unaffected, and the change is favourable to us.
The fee exposure under 4.2(a) where the Company terminates for HDI's breach is correctly reserved to a cause/remedies rule rather than double-flagged here.
